summary.intent: Execute Phase 70.1 (rotation read-plane durability + deep crash-resume soundness) end-to-end for CipherBox: run wave-based parallel worktree execution of 13 plans, close the D-16 desktop-e2e human checkpoint, verify the phase, and run the full autonomous ship-phase flow (secure/validate/simplify/SDK-E2E/CodeRabbit/PR) before shipping.
summary.outcome: All 13 plans merged and gated green; D-16 desktop-e2e acceptance passed on macOS, Linux, and Windows after fixing a revocation-bypass security bug, a double-publish bug, and a macOS idle-mount publish-queue stall. Phase verification (7/8 SCs code-confirmed, SC#6 closed via live sdk-e2e), security audit (SECURED, 33/33 threats resolved), Nyquist validation (8/8 compliant), and simplify review all passed; ship-phase flow was mid-way through CodeRabbit-driven fixes (2 more real bugs found and fixed: fail-open child-list override causing silent data loss, and a dormant crash-resume soundness gap in both TS and Rust engines) when the transcript ends, with commits staged but PR not yet opened.

repo: gsd commit helper frequently reports 'commit_failed' as a false negative even when the commit lands — always verify with `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry.

rust-analyzer diagnostics (E0063 missing field, dead_code, unresolved macro references) are frequently stale mid-edit snapshots during concurrent agent edits — always confirm with authoritative `cargo check`/`cargo test` before trusting them.

`cargo fmt --all` run by an executor strands out-of-scope formatting drift across the whole workspace; always scope to `cargo fmt -p <crate>` and revert any accidental workspace-wide drift before committing.
Cross-package dist staleness causes false test failures: after changing sdk-core in one wave, must rebuild sdk-core AND its consumer (sdk) dist before the consumer's vitest suite reflects the change.
desktop-e2e CI has two separate harnesses per platform: macOS/Linux run `run-all.sh`, Windows runs `run-all.ps1` — a new step must be added to both or Windows silently skips it.

sdk-e2e vitest has no dotenv loader; running it outside CI requires manually sourcing `apps/api/.env` (`set -a; . ./.env; set +a`) or the harness silently falls back to a default TEST_LOGIN_SECRET and 401s.

macOS FUSE-T defers `release()` by ~40s and ignores the `inval_inode` reverse-notification, so the local publish-queue (edge-triggered, no backstop) and the SMB read-side cache invalidation are both structurally fragile on macOS relative to Linux fuser.

tee-republish.test.ts requires the TEE worker's `tee_key_state` to be separately seeded/initialized on :3002 — failing fast with 'tee_key_state is empty' is a local-stack precondition issue, not a code fault.

Root `SECURITY.md` is the legitimate committed project policy (#482); the gsd security auditor should write the phase-specific `<phase>-SECURITY.md` instead — must verify this before running the auditor to avoid clobbering it.

The GSD decision-coverage gate parser only accepts three `- **D-NN...**` bullet forms; a bullet using `(title).**` (period before closing bold) fails to parse and silently zeroes out coverage for ALL decisions in the file, not just the malformed one.

code.finding: collectDirtyFrontier originally AEAD-decrypted a child's sealed ref with the parent's current key BEFORE checking plaintext generation to determine dirtiness — for a genuinely-dirty edge where the parent also rotated, decrypt always throws before the check runs. Fixed by comparing childPub.generation > childRef.generation first and pushing dirty edges with nodeReadKey: undefined, deferring key recovery to repairDirtyNode via the ECIES checkpoint.
Rust twin of the same decrypt-before-dirtiness-check ordering bug in collect_dirty_frontier; fixed identically.

rotate_read_on_scope_exit discarded the RotateReadResult and never refreshed the grant-root inode's in-memory read_key, so a subsequent relink republish resealed the folder under the STALE pre-rotation key and published it last — allowing the revoked recipient to still decrypt. Fixed via refresh_grant_root_read_key which copies the new key into the inode in place before any relink.

build_scope_exit_child_override (used for coalesced scope-exit publish) failed OPEN per-child: a missing child inode or a build_child_refs error silently dropped that child from the override list, and the override REPLACES the grant-root's published children — causing silent orphaning/invisibility of a sibling on rotation. Fixed to error (propagate via ?) on those cases, mirroring the fail-closed discipline of build_folder_metadata, with the caller mapping the Err to EIO.

The Skipped-branch resume path discarded the is_dirty signal from verify_subtree_clean and only checked frontier.is_empty() to decide convergence — a missing root returns {is_dirty:true, frontier:[]}, so it would be mis-marked Complete instead of routed to the fail-closed resolve path. Currently dormant (FUSE's persist_job is a no-op so no resume path exists yet) but latent for TS's web rotation which does persist. Fixed in both engines by capturing the full outcome and gating the short-circuit on !is_dirty.

CipherBoxFS held three independent JsonSidecarFloorStore instances over the same rotation-high-water.json sidecar, each constructing its own Arc<Mutex<()>>, while write_map_atomic_blocking used a shared deterministic .tmp path — causing a rename ENOENT race between concurrent writers. Fixed with a process-global path-keyed lock registry (shared_lock_for) so all instances over the same path serialize.

Publish-queue drain (flush_publish_queue) is edge-triggered only from FUSE op handlers with no wall-clock backstop; on an idle mount (esp. macOS where release is deferred), a queued parent republish never fires. Fixed with a background 'fuse-publish-pump' thread doing periodic unique-name lookups every 2s to drive the drain, bounded to mount lifetime via an AtomicBool flag.

workflow: When challenged on whether all N plans of a wave are running concurrently, verify: harness backgrounds every dispatched agent regardless of 'synchronous' framing, so a perceived serial dispatch may already be running in parallel underneath — check worktree creation timestamps to confirm.

Simultaneous `git worktree add` calls race on `.git/config.lock`; dispatch worktree-creating agents one-per-message rather than in a single parallel batch, then let them run concurrently once created.

Hold pushes/CI dispatches until multiple independent fixes (e.g. WinFsp coalescing + macOS drain fix) are all ready, then batch into one CI round-trip rather than burning multiple 15-40min real-mount runs.

Use a resumed debugger/fixer agent (SendMessage) rather than a fresh one when it already holds deep root-cause context (repro setup, instrumentation, file locations) — much cheaper than re-deriving context.

CodeRabbit CLI findings should be adversarially re-verified (via a dedicated reviewer agent) against the actual current code before applying fixes — CLI findings can misattribute root cause or overstate live reachability (e.g. calling a dormant bug 'critical').

When a fix required for TS/Rust engine parity is discovered while fixing one engine, apply it to both engines even if only one was flagged — otherwise the reference/twin relationship the phase enforces breaks.

Distinguishing CI infra flakes (e.g. Windows STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED before the API even started) from real test failures requires reading the actual failing step, not just the overall run conclusion — re-run only the failed job rather than the whole matrix.

An orphaned rust-analyzer process consuming multiple GB of RAM can be traced to its parent process (a leftover 'claude --dangerously-skip-permissions' session bound to an already-deleted worktree) via `ps` parent-PID inspection and CWD lookup.

friction: Wrong skill name guessed first (`gsd-ship-phase` instead of `ship-phase`) before locating the correct one.
Multiple rounds of stale rust-analyzer diagnostics (E0063, dead_code, unresolved macro) required repeated authoritative `cargo check`/`cargo test` re-verification, consuming time on false alarms.
cleanup-wave blocked on Wave 1 merge due to plan 03's unscoped `cargo fmt --all` leaving out-of-scope drift in the worktree — required manual discard before merge could proceed.
Wave 3 post-merge gate showed 3 false test failures due to cross-package dist staleness (sdk-core changed but sdk consumer dist not rebuilt) before being correctly diagnosed.

D-16 desktop-e2e acceptance required four full CI round-trips (each ~15-40 min) across multiple root-cause/fix cycles: initial 2-defect diagnosis (double-publish + revocation bypass), WinFsp parity gap, macOS setup timeout, and a transient Windows STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED infra flake requiring a job re-run.
THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET missing from apps/api/.env during the ship-phase SDK-E2E gate run — proceeded without it since throttling shouldn't bite in a single serial run, but it's a latent gap.

2/3 Rust rotation engine test suites (tee-republish) failed during the ship-phase SDK-E2E run due to an unrelated local-stack precondition (TEE worker not initialized), requiring investigation to confirm it wasn't a phase regression.

11GB of RAM consumed by two rust-analyzer processes, one an orphan from a leftover Phase-69 session bound to an already-deleted worktree — surfaced mid-flow and had to be diagnosed and cleaned up without derailing the ship-phase work.
